title: Instructions for a Rice Cooker
body:
A rice cooker is an electric pot with a heating plate, a removable inner pot, and a lid. It brings rice and water to a boil, then switches itself to a warm setting when the water is absorbed.

Setup

  1. Put the cooker on a flat, stable, heat-safe surface near an outlet.
  2. Wash the inner pot and dry the outside so no water drips onto the heating plate.
  3. Measure rice with the cooker's cup and rinse it until the water runs mostly clear.
  4. Add water to the marked line for your rice amount.
  5. Seat the inner pot flat on the heating plate and close the lid.

How to operate it

  1. Plug in the cooker and press the cook switch down.
  2. Leave the lid closed while it cooks; lifting it lets steam and heat escape.
  3. Wait for the cooker to click over to warm on its own.
  4. Leave it on warm for ten minutes so the rice finishes steaming.
  5. Fluff the rice with the paddle and serve.

Care and maintenance

Wash the inner pot and lid after each use and wipe the heating plate when cool. Never immerse the cooker body in water. Descale or wipe away any starch film so the plate stays flat against the pot.

Common problems and fixes

  • Rice sticks or burns: Rinse the rice better and check the water line; a warped pot or dirty plate also causes hot spots.
  • Rice is undercooked: The lid may have been lifted during cooking; keep it closed and rest on warm longer.

Safety

The pot, lid, and steam are hot. Keep the steam vent away from your face and hands, and never cook with the lid open.

Settings check

  • Lid: closed
  • Inner pot: seated
  • Mode: cook

title: Instructions for a Pressure Cooker
body:
A pressure cooker is a sealed pot that cooks with trapped steam at high pressure. It cooks beans, stews, and tough cuts far faster than an open pot, but it must seal correctly and must never be forced open while pressurised.

Setup

  1. Check the sealing ring: clean, flexible, and seated evenly in the lid groove.
  2. Check the steam valve moves freely and the float valve is clean.
  3. Add food plus at least the minimum liquid the maker requires, usually one cup.
  4. Close the lid until it locks and set the valve to sealing.
  5. Place the cooker on a stable burner or base, handles clear of other burners.

How to operate it

  1. Heat on medium-high until the cooker reaches pressure and the float valve rises.
  2. Lower the heat to hold steady pressure and start the recipe time.
  3. When time is up, turn off the heat.
  4. Release pressure as the recipe directs: natural release by waiting, or quick release by moving the valve carefully.
  5. Wait until the float valve drops, which means pressure is fully gone, then open the lid away from your face.

Care and maintenance

Wash the pot, lid, ring, and valves after use and dry them fully. Replace a stretched or cracked sealing ring. Never store the cooker with the lid locked on; keep the ring loose so it keeps its shape.

Common problems and fixes

  • It never reaches pressure: The ring may be unseated or worn, or there may be too little liquid.
  • Steam leaks around the lid: Stop heating, release pressure safely, and reseat or replace the ring.

Safety

Never force a lid open while the float valve is up. Keep hands and face away from the steam valve during release. Never fill past the maximum line, and never heat an empty cooker.

Settings check

  • Sealing ring: seated
  • Valve: sealed
  • Liquid present: yes

title: Instructions for a Slow Cooker
body:
A slow cooker is an electric crock pot that cooks food gently for hours on low or high. It is made for unattended cooking of stews, soups, and braises.

Setup

  1. Put the cooker on a flat, heat-safe surface away from the counter edge.
  2. Place the crock in the base and check it sits level.
  3. Add ingredients, keeping food below the rim, and add enough liquid to cover the base.
  4. Put the lid on straight so it seals all around.
  5. Plug in and choose low or high as the recipe directs.

How to operate it

  1. Start cooking and leave the lid on; every lift adds cooking time.
  2. Cook for the recipe's time, usually four to eight hours on low.
  3. Check near the end only if the recipe asks for it.
  4. Turn the cooker off before serving.
  5. Serve from the crock or ladle out, using mitts for the hot crock.

Care and maintenance

Wash the crock and lid with warm soapy water once cool; wipe the base, never immersing it. Soak stuck food instead of scraping the crock. Store with the lid ajar so it stays fresh.

Common problems and fixes

  • Food is undercooked: The lid was likely lifted often; keep it closed and add time.
  • Food is dry: Use more liquid next time and check the lid seals flat.

Safety

The crock and lid stay hot for a long time. Use mitts, keep the cord away from the counter edge, and never cook with a cracked crock.

Settings check

  • Lid: on
  • Setting: low
  • Liquid covers base: yes

title: Instructions for a Toaster Oven
body:
A toaster oven is a small countertop oven for toasting, baking, and reheating. It heats faster than a full oven and suits small portions.

Setup

  1. Put the oven on a flat, heat-safe surface with space around it for airflow.
  2. Remove all packaging and wash the rack and tray.
  3. Slide the crumb tray fully in and centre the rack for your dish.
  4. Plug in directly, not through a loose extension lead.
  5. Run it empty for a few minutes first if the maker advises burning off factory coatings.

How to operate it

  1. Choose the mode: toast, bake, or broil, as your food needs.
  2. Set the temperature and time, then wait for the ready light if fitted.
  3. Put food on the rack or tray and close the door.
  4. Watch through the window near the end; small ovens brown fast.
  5. When done, turn it off, open the door carefully, and remove food with mitts.

Care and maintenance

Empty the crumb tray regularly; crumbs near the elements can smoke or catch fire. Wipe the interior when cool and wash the tray and rack. Never spray cleaner into the elements or vents.

Common problems and fixes

  • Toast browns unevenly: Centre the food and turn it halfway through.
  • It smokes: Turn it off, let it cool, and clean the crumb tray and interior.

Safety

The outside and door get hot. Keep curtains, paper, and towels away, never leave it running unattended, and never put foil against the elements unless the maker allows it.

Settings check

  • Rack: centered
  • Mode: bake
  • Timer: set

title: Instructions for a Vacuum Cleaner
body:
A vacuum cleaner is a motorised cleaner that pulls dust and dirt into a bag or bin through a brush head. Regular emptying and filter care keep its suction strong.

Setup

  1. Unwrap the cord fully and plug in, keeping the cord behind you.
  2. Check the bag or bin: empty it if it is more than two-thirds full.
  3. Check the filter is clean and seated, and the brush head spins freely.
  4. Set the head height for your floor type: lower for hard floors and thin carpet, higher for deep carpet.
  5. Clear the floor of cords, small toys, and anything that could jam the brush.

How to operate it

  1. Switch on and push forward in slow, overlapping passes.
  2. Overlap each pass by about half the head width.
  3. For carpet, make a slow forward pass then pull back over the same strip.
  4. Use the hose and tools for edges, stairs, and furniture.
  5. Switch off, unplug by the plug, and wind the cord before storing.

Care and maintenance

Empty the bin or change the bag before it packs full. Wash or replace filters as the maker directs, and cut hair and thread off the brushroll. Check the hose for blockages when suction drops.

Common problems and fixes

  • Suction is weak: Empty the bin, clean the filter, and check the hose and head for blockages.
  • It smells musty: Clean or replace the filter and empty the bin; never vacuum damp material unless the machine is made for it.

Safety

Never vacuum liquids, hot ash, or sharp objects unless the machine is rated for them. Keep fingers, hair, and loose clothing away from the brushroll, and unplug before clearing a jam.

Settings check

  • Bag or bin: ok
  • Filter: clean
  • Brushroll: free

title: Instructions for a Steam Mop
body:
A steam mop is a floor cleaner that turns water into steam and pushes it through a cloth pad. It cleans sealed hard floors without detergents.

Setup

  1. Fill the tank with plain water only, up to the marked line, unless the maker says otherwise.
  2. Attach a clean mop pad firmly to the head.
  3. Plug in on a hard floor and let it heat until the ready light shows.
  4. Test on a small hidden area first.
  5. Keep the cord behind you and the floor clear of rugs you do not want steamed.

How to operate it

  1. Press the steam trigger or button and push forward slowly.
  2. Move in overlapping passes so every strip gets steam.
  3. Pause on stubborn spots for a few seconds instead of scrubbing hard.
  4. When the pad gets dirty, stop, let the head cool briefly, and fit a clean pad.
  5. When finished, switch off, unplug, and let the mop cool before emptying the tank.

Care and maintenance

Wash pads after each use and let them dry fully. Empty the tank after use so it cannot grow stale. Descale as the maker directs if your water is hard. Replace worn pads that no longer grip.

Common problems and fixes

  • It leaves streaks: Slow down and fit a clean pad; a dirty pad spreads dirt.
  • Little or no steam: Check the water level and let it fully heat; check the pad is not blocking the vents.

Safety

Steam burns. Never point the head at feet, pets, or people, and never use it on unsealed wood, waxed floors, or laminate unless the maker allows it.

Settings check

  • Tank: filled
  • Pad: attached
  • Floor type: hard

title: Instructions for a Humidifier
body:
A humidifier is a device that adds moisture to indoor air. It eases dry air in winter and helps with dry skin and irritated airways when used and cleaned properly.

Setup

  1. Put the humidifier on a flat, waterproof surface at least a metre from the bed and electronics.
  2. Fill the tank with clean, cool water, preferably distilled if your water is hard.
  3. Fit the filter or wick if your model uses one.
  4. Seat the tank firmly and close any caps.
  5. Plug in and set the output to a comfortable level.

How to operate it

  1. Switch on and let it run until the room feels comfortable.
  2. Aim for indoor humidity around forty to fifty percent; use a hygrometer if you have one.
  3. Refill the tank when it runs low, switching off first.
  4. Turn it down or off if windows start to mist heavily.
  5. Switch off and unplug before moving or refilling.

Care and maintenance

Empty, rinse, and dry the tank daily, and deep-clean weekly as the maker directs. Replace filters on schedule. A dirty humidifier can spread mould and bacteria, so cleaning is not optional.

Common problems and fixes

  • White dust appears: Your tap water is hard; switch to distilled water and clean the tank.
  • The room feels damp: Lower the output or run it for shorter periods.

Safety

Keep it away from bedding and electronics, never let water pool under it, and keep it out of children's reach when it uses warm steam. Stop using it if it smells musty after cleaning.

Settings check

  • Tank: filled
  • Filter: clean
  • Humidity target: 45

title: Instructions for an Air Purifier
body:
An air purifier is a fan-driven filter unit that pulls room air through filters to trap dust, pollen, and smoke particles. It helps most in a closed room with the right size unit.

Setup

  1. Put the purifier where air can flow freely around it, away from walls and curtains.
  2. Remove all filter packaging before first use.
  3. Seat each filter in the correct order and close the cover fully.
  4. Plug in and check the air-quality light or display works.
  5. Close windows and doors in the room for best results.

How to operate it

  1. Switch on and set the fan to medium for everyday use.
  2. Use high speed when cooking smoke or dust is present, then drop back to medium.
  3. Use sleep or quiet mode at night if fitted.
  4. Check the filter-life indicator monthly.
  5. Replace filters when the indicator says so, or on the maker's schedule.

Care and maintenance

Vacuum the pre-filter gently as directed and replace main filters on time; a clogged filter cuts airflow and cleaning power. Wipe the outside with a dry cloth. Keep the intake and outlet clear of dust build-up.

Common problems and fixes

  • Airflow feels weak: Check the filters: a clogged filter is the usual cause.
  • It rattles: Reseat the filters and cover until they click in place.

Safety

Never block the intake or outlet, never run it with the cover open, and unplug before changing filters. It does not remove gases like carbon monoxide; keep working alarms fitted.

Settings check

  • Filter: seated
  • Fan speed: medium
  • Intake: clear

title: Instructions for a Space Heater
body:
A space heater is a portable electric heater for warming one room. It is useful for short periods in a cold room, but it needs clear space and attention because it runs hot.

Setup

  1. Put the heater on a flat, hard floor, never on a bed, rug edge, or wobbly table.
  2. Clear at least one metre around it, including curtains, paper, and furniture.
  3. Plug it directly into a wall outlet, never into an extension lead or power strip.
  4. Set the thermostat to medium to start.
  5. Check the tip-over switch and overheat protection are fitted and working.

How to operate it

  1. Switch on and set the thermostat to the comfort level you want.
  2. Let the room warm up, then turn the thermostat down to hold the temperature.
  3. Keep the room door closed so heat stays in.
  4. Turn it off when you leave the room or go to sleep, unless it is specifically made for unattended use and the maker says so.
  5. Unplug it when not in use for a long stretch.

Care and maintenance

Dust the intake and outlet regularly when cool and unplugged. Check the cord for damage before each season. Replace the heater if it smells of burning after cleaning or if the thermostat behaves erratically.

Common problems and fixes

  • It trips the breaker: It may share a circuit with other heavy loads; move it to another circuit and unplug other heaters.
  • It cycles on and off constantly: The thermostat may sit in a draught; move the heater slightly and reset the thermostat.

Safety

Never leave a space heater running unattended or while sleeping unless the maker explicitly allows it. Keep children and pets from touching it, never dry clothes on it, and never use it in a bathroom unless it is rated for that.

Settings check

  • Clearance: 1m
  • Surface: flat
  • Thermostat: medium

title: Instructions for a Combination Lock
body:
A combination lock is a lock opened by turning a dial to a sequence of numbers, with no key. It is used on padlocks, lockers, and safes.

Setup

  1. Learn your combination and store it somewhere safe, not on the lock.
  2. Start with the dial at zero and the shackle closed.
  3. Practise the turning pattern slowly before you rely on it.
  4. Check the shackle clicks shut when you close it.
  5. Scramble the dial after locking so the numbers do not sit on the combination.

How to operate it

  1. Turn the dial clockwise three full turns to clear it, stopping on the first number.
  2. Turn counter-clockwise one full turn past the first number, stopping on the second number.
  3. Turn clockwise directly to the third number.
  4. Pull the shackle or handle to open.
  5. To lock again, close the shackle and scramble the dial.

Care and maintenance

Keep the dial clean and dry; blow out dust rather than oiling it, since oil attracts grit. If it stiffens, use a tiny amount of graphite lubricant made for locks. Never force a jammed dial.

Common problems and fixes

  • It will not open: Clear the dial with three full clockwise turns and retry slowly; most failures come from rushing the second number.
  • The dial feels gritty: Clean it dry and add graphite lubricant, not oil.

Safety

Never share your combination, and change it if anyone else learns it. A combination lock is a deterrent, not a guarantee; pair it with good storage habits for valuables.

Settings check

  • Dial: zero
  • Combination: known
  • Shackle: closed

title: Instructions for a Can Opener
body:
A can opener is a hand tool that cuts the lid off a metal food can. A good one cuts cleanly and leaves a safe edge.

Setup

  1. Wash the can top so dirt cannot fall into the food.
  2. Check the opener's cutting wheel is clean and sharp.
  3. Place the opener on the can rim with the wheel on top of the lid edge.
  4. Squeeze the handles so the wheel bites into the lid.
  5. Keep the can on a stable surface.

How to operate it

  1. Turn the handle steadily so the wheel travels around the lid.
  2. Keep even pressure; do not jerk the opener.
  3. When the cut is complete, lift the lid carefully by its edge.
  4. Pour or spoon out the food.
  5. Rinse the opener and dry it before storing.

Care and maintenance

Wash and dry the opener after each use so food does not dry onto the wheel. Oil the hinge occasionally with food-safe oil if it stiffens. Replace the opener when the wheel slips or leaves jagged edges.

Common problems and fixes

  • The wheel slips: Re-seat it on the rim and squeeze firmly before turning again.
  • The lid tears jaggedly: The wheel is dull; replace the opener.

Safety

Cut lids are sharp. Lift them by the edge, keep fingers away from the cut rim, and discard lids safely where children cannot reach them.

Settings check

  • Blade: clean
  • Wheel: aligned
  • Can: stable

title: Instructions for a Corkscrew
body:
A corkscrew is a tool for pulling the cork out of a wine bottle. A waiter's corkscrew with a lever is the most reliable common type.

Setup

  1. Cut the foil below the bottle lip and peel it away.
  2. Wipe the bottle top clean.
  3. Open the corkscrew's lever and screw fully.
  4. Hold the bottle steady on a flat surface.
  5. Check the cork is not crumbling before you start.

How to operate it

  1. Place the screw tip in the centre of the cork.
  2. Twist straight down until only one turn of screw shows.
  3. Fold the lever onto the bottle lip as a fulcrum.
  4. Pull the handle up steadily to draw the cork out.
  5. If the cork resists, reset the lever to the second step if fitted and pull again.

Care and maintenance

Wipe the screw after use and dry it before folding it away. Keep it closed when stored so the screw cannot snag or cut. Replace it if the screw bends or the lever loosens.

Common problems and fixes

  • The cork breaks apart: Screw in again carefully and pull slowly; for old corks, use a two-prong puller if you have one.
  • The screw goes in crooked: Back it out and restart dead centre.

Safety

The screw is sharp. Keep fingers clear of the tip, never force a stuck cork with a knife, and keep broken glass and cork pieces away from the drink.

Settings check

  • Foil: removed
  • Screw: centered
  • Lever: seated

title: Instructions for a Glue Gun
body:
A glue gun is a handheld tool that melts solid glue sticks and squeezes out hot liquid glue for crafts and light repairs. It bonds fast but the glue and nozzle are very hot.

Setup

  1. Put the gun on its stand on a heat-safe surface with scrap paper underneath.
  2. Load a glue stick of the correct size into the back.
  3. Plug in and wait until the ready light shows or glue flows easily.
  4. Have your pieces ready and positioned before you start, since the glue sets fast.
  5. Keep a damp cloth nearby for drips.

How to operate it

  1. Squeeze the trigger gently to lay a thin line of glue where you want the bond.
  2. Press the pieces together at once and hold for about thirty seconds.
  3. Do not move the joint while it cools.
  4. Wipe stray strings of glue away while still warm, with care.
  5. When finished, unplug the gun and leave it on its stand to cool.

Care and maintenance

Wipe the nozzle when cool and remove drips from the stand. Never leave a hot gun on its side. Replace the nozzle if it clogs badly, and store sticks dry. Unplug between sessions rather than leaving it heated for hours.

Common problems and fixes

  • Glue will not flow: Check the gun is fully heated and the stick is the right size and fully pushed in.
  • Bonds pop apart: The surfaces may be dusty or the glue may have cooled before pressing; clean surfaces and press at once.

Safety

Hot glue burns skin. Never touch the nozzle or fresh glue, keep the gun away from children, and never point it at yourself or others. Work in a ventilated area.

Settings check

  • Stick: loaded
  • Nozzle: clear
  • Stand: stable

title: Instructions for an Extension Ladder
body:
An extension ladder is a two-section ladder that slides longer for reaching roofs and high walls. Safe use depends on the angle, the footing, and never overreaching.

Setup

  1. Check the ladder for bent rungs, cracked rails, and working locks before use.
  2. Set it on firm, level ground, never on soft soil or a slope without levelling.
  3. Extend it so it reaches about one metre above the surface you will step onto.
  4. Set the angle with the one-to-four rule: the base sits one unit out for every four units of height.
  5. Tie or secure the top if you can, and have someone foot the ladder for long climbs.

How to operate it

  1. Face the ladder and climb with three points of contact at all times: two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand.
  2. Carry tools on a belt or hoist them up; never carry them in your hands while climbing.
  3. Work with your belt buckle inside the rails; never lean out sideways.
  4. Move the ladder instead of overreaching.
  5. Climb down the same way, facing the ladder, before moving it.

Care and maintenance

Clean mud and paint off rungs and locks, and store the ladder flat or hung, out of weather. Check ropes, pulleys, and locks each season. Retire a ladder with bent rails or failed locks.

Common problems and fixes

  • The ladder feels wobbly: Climb down, re-level the feet, and reset the angle; never wedge one foot with loose material.
  • The sections will not lock: Clean the locks and rungs; if a lock is damaged, stop using the ladder.

Safety

Never use a metal ladder near power lines. Never stand on the top three rungs, never overreach, and never climb in high wind or rain. If you feel dizzy or unsure, climb down.

Settings check

  • Angle: 75deg
  • Feet: level
  • Top: secured

title: Instructions for Binoculars
body:
Binoculars are a pair of small telescopes joined together for viewing distant objects with both eyes. Good setup means matching them to your eyes and focus before you look.

Setup

  1. Remove the lens caps and check the lenses are clean.
  2. Adjust the hinge so the two circles merge into one when you look through.
  3. Set the diopter, usually on the right eyepiece, for your eyesight difference.
  4. Put the neck strap on so a drop cannot damage them.
  5. Start with the focus wheel centred.

How to operate it

  1. Raise the binoculars to your eyes and adjust the hinge until you see one full circle.
  2. Close your right eye and focus the left side sharply with the centre wheel.
  3. Open both eyes, close the left eye, and adjust the right diopter until sharp.
  4. Now use only the centre wheel for distance changes.
  5. Hold steady by bracing your elbows or resting against support for long looks.

Care and maintenance

Brush dust off lenses before wiping, and wipe with a lens cloth only. Store with caps on in the case, away from heat and damp. Never leave them in a hot car, which can damage seals and coatings.

Common problems and fixes

  • You see two overlapping circles: Adjust the hinge width until they merge into one.
  • One side stays blurry: Reset the diopter for that eye and refocus with the centre wheel.

Safety

Never look at the sun through binoculars; it can blind you instantly. Keep the strap on around water and heights, and keep them away from small children unsupervised.

Settings check

  • Lens caps: off
  • Diopter: adjusted
  • Focus: sharp

title: Instructions for a Paper Shredder
body:
A paper shredder is a machine that cuts documents into strips or particles for privacy. It works best within its sheet limit and with regular oiling.

Setup

  1. Put the shredder on a flat surface with the bin fully seated under the head.
  2. Plug in and set the switch to auto, so it starts when paper enters.
  3. Remove staples and clips if your model does not rate for them.
  4. Count sheets to stay within the maker's sheet limit.
  5. Keep fingers, ties, and loose sleeves away from the feed slot.

How to operate it

  1. Feed sheets straight into the slot, a few at a time, within the limit.
  2. Let the machine finish and stop before feeding more.
  3. If it slows or strains, stop and feed fewer sheets.
  4. Use reverse briefly if paper jams, then forward again.
  5. Empty the bin before it packs against the cutters.

Care and maintenance

Oil the cutters regularly with shredder oil as the maker directs; dry paper dust wears them fast. Empty the bin often and wipe the feed slot clean. Unplug before clearing any jam by hand.

Common problems and fixes

  • It jams: Switch to reverse, remove the jammed sheets, then feed fewer sheets.
  • It runs but shreds poorly: Oil the cutters and empty a packed bin.

Safety

Keep fingers, hair, and clothing away from the feed slot at all times. Never let children use it unsupervised, and unplug it before reaching near the cutters.

Settings check

  • Bin: empty
  • Sheet count: within
  • Power: on
